浜松餃子.summary: Fried in a circle in the pan and served with boiled bean sprouts in the middle. The light, cabbage-rich filling makes them easy to keep eating. Eat them with the bean sprouts in the center to refresh your palate.

富士宮やきそば.summary: Firm, chewy steamed noodles topped with crispy pork bits (nikukasu) and sardine or mackerel powder (dashiko). Made famous by winning the B-1 Grand Prix. Locals sprinkle plenty of dashiko on top. A perfect stop on a trip to see Mt. Fuji.

shops.name: Fujinomiya Yakisoba Antenna Shop
shops.query: 富士宮やきそばアンテナショップ
shops.comment: Near Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha shrine. A good place to compare styles.
shops.access: In front of Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha (Omiya Yokocho)

静岡おでん.summary: Oden simmered in a dark broth made with beef tendon, with every ingredient on a skewer. The grey kuro hanpen fish cake made from sardines or mackerel is a must. Sprinkle on fish powder and green seaweed flakes. Try it at old-style candy shops or izakaya.

shops.name: Aoba Oden Street
shops.query: 青葉おでん街 静岡
shops.comment: An alley lined with Shizuoka oden bars. Fun for bar-hopping.
shops.access: Central Shizuoka City (around Aoba Symbol Road)

生しらす丼.summary: A rice bowl piled with raw whitebait caught in Suruga Bay. Freshness is everything, so it is best eaten in the fishing towns where it is landed. Raw whitebait may not be served during the winter-to-spring closed season or on days when boats cannot go out.

三島コロッケ.summary: Croquettes made with Mishima-grown potatoes, known for their fluffy texture and natural sweetness. A local snack to eat while strolling.

浜名湖うな重.summary: Grilled eel over rice served in a lacquered box, from the area around Lake Hamana, a major center of eel farming. Popular restaurants can sell out before noon, so go early.

サクラエビのかき揚げ.summary: A crispy fritter packed with sakura shrimp, which in Japan are landed only in Suruga Bay. Fragrant, crunchy and naturally sweet. The fishing seasons are spring and autumn, when you can also try them raw or boiled.

金目の煮付け.summary: Splendid alfonsino, a red-skinned fish Izu is famous for, simmered in a sweet soy sauce glaze. The tender white flesh goes perfectly with rice.

とろろ汁.summary: Grated wild yam thinned with miso soup and poured over barley rice. A specialty of Mariko, an old post town on the Tokaido road.

山葵漬け.summary: Chopped wasabi pickled in sake lees, a Shizuoka specialty with a sharp kick. Great with rice, sashimi or fish cakes.

うなぎパイ.summary: Crispy pie cookies made with eel extract by Hamamatsu confectioner Shunkado. The classic Hamamatsu souvenir.
うなぎパイ.area: Hamamatsu and souvenir shops across the prefecture

安倍川もち.summary: Soft, freshly pounded rice cakes coated in roasted soybean flour (kinako) or smooth red bean paste, sold by teahouses along the Abe River for centuries.

こっこ.summary: A fluffy steamed sponge cake filled with milk cream, and one of Shizuoka's best-known souvenirs.
こっこ.area: Stations and souvenir shops across the prefecture

治一郎のバウムクーヘン.summary: A Hamamatsu-born baumkuchen loved for its moist texture. People travel from outside the prefecture to buy it.
